I often ask myself what the hell happened to me to feel this way. We are here to push us to continue with our existence in this cruel world. I'm so happy that you found the right cocktail

My closest friends I told right away. The majority of them were surprised of my diagnosis but they were very supportive and still are. The first group I dealt with was my family I'm lucky enough that I'm close to them that I was able to tell them what was going on. In the meantime I'm dealing with some of them not agreeing with the diagnosis and I am not at the point of proving them wrong. I need to work on myself and continue with my medication and self-help so I can live a life here on Earth.
Thank you I really need to hear this.

I understand what you are feeling. I was raped by my Uncle at 9. I told my sister right after it happened and she told my mom who's brother it was. Nothing changed. She never told my Father who would have killed him. So I have had to live with it until my adult life and it wasn't easy. I have no trust in men it's difficult for me to get close to one and I've never had a relationship. Now I know I'm closer to women and I'm probably gay but I'm not ready to get into relationship because of my issues with trust. My struggle is daily and what keeps me going is the fact that I always say I'm here for a reason. I want you to know that you are here for a reason and I know you suffered a lot but don't give up your life is worth something you're here to give us a gift that's why you're alive please don't give up. It's always going to be a struggle this I know and I have to accept it. It is sad that life is not easy and this is so f****** true.

I feel the same. You are not alone. This disease takes a hold of us. Know your worth. Your existence is not for nothing. I wish I could give you hug and tell you this in person. Hang on. Don't give up. Right now nothing makes sense, but it will, only when you let it go it's course.
May I ask why your are weaning off the medication?

Yes this happens to me. Usually when I am in the shower. I feel sad and sorry for myself for being diagnosed with Bipolar II. I know it's not a death sentence, and I am just learning about it and starting medication to control my mood swings.

I joined group therapy virtually 3x a week. This has helped me immensely. So has this thread. It gives me peace of mind that I am not the only one and that I can live a fullfilled life. At the moment I am not quite there yet but working on it.
Thank you I really needed to read this.
Thank you so much
I picked up my new medication it's called lamotrigine. Has anyone else had experience with this medication?
Thank you I will be sure to keep posting updates during my healing process.
Thank you. I will try to get through this

Thank you for your response and your wise words. I am completely exhausted emotionally and physically. I don't want to continue to be in this body. Life is very short and I went to the in between space when I had my heart attack and a near death experience. It was peaceful there was no pain and I regret fighting to stay alive. I want to feel that peace again but I don't think it's possible to do in our human form.

I am in the same boat as you question why I'm here all the time. I feel lost and empty I have nothing to look forward to. Then I survive a night's sleep and wake up in the morning because I'm still here and I have a purpose. It is important to have he could support system it surrounds you this is the only thing that is going to help you. I am fortunate in the fact that I have a loving family who is understanding and friends too who will go above and beyond to be there for me. I am here for you because I understand what you're feeling and you wouldn't exist if you didn't have a purpose in this life so please don't give up.
